title: The Book of Joel
lead: A three-chapter book of the Twelve that begins with a plague of locusts and a call to fast, turns on the LORD's words "Even now, turn back to me", and looks ahead to the Spirit poured out on all flesh and the nations judged in the Valley of Jehoshaphat. Peter quotes it at Pentecost.

sections.b: Joel is quoted or echoed in the Old and New Testaments more than its size would suggest. Joel 2:13 (the creed with "he changes his mind about the harm") is shared with Jonah 4:2. Joel 3:16 and 3:18 are matched in Amos 1:2 and 9:13. Joel 1:15 is Isaiah 13:6. Peter quotes Joel 2:28-32 at Pentecost (Acts 2:17-21), Paul quotes 2:32 in Romans 10:13, and Revelation uses Joel's locusts (Revelation 9:7-9), sun and moon (Revelation 6:12) and harvest and winepress (Revelation 14:14-20).
sections.refs: Joel 2:13; Jonah 4:2; Joel 3:16; Amos 1:2; Isaiah 13:6; Acts 2:17-21; Romans 10:13; Revelation 9:7-9; Revelation 14:14-20

sections.b: The book names no king and gives no date. The two main proposals are the ninth century BC, in the days of the boy-king Joash, and the Persian period, in the fifth or fourth century BC. Neither is proved, and the topic pages treat Joel's themes without needing the answer.
